subject: Hosted API renewal — monthly throughput increase & rate-floor discussion
messages:

Subject: Hosted API renewal — request to raise monthly throughput and burst window

Hi Marissa,

Quick context: Parklane's recommmerce feature is launching a larger personalization sweep for Q4 and we expect sustained traffic increases starting September. We're approaching renewal in August and want to evaluate increasing our monthly committed throughput and a larger burst allowance for peak windows.

Current contract: 40M tokens/month committed, 4x burst for short windows.
Our ask: explore options to move to 90M tokens/month committed (12-month term), with a larger burst pocket for seasonal spikes (Black Friday/Cyber Monday). We need: pricing for the 90M tier, any stepped-rate floors if we tier usage, proposed rate limits per route, and any potential credits for overage or temporary throttling windows.

Attached is our procurement request doc (Parklane_Q2_Procurement_Request.pdf) with timelines and the PO cadence. Can we get a ballpark commercial and an ops plan by EOD Friday? We'd like to schedule a 30m call with engineering to align on routing/latency expectations.

Thanks — Asha

Hi Asha — thanks for the note and the procurement doc. This is a good problem to solve; congrats on the feature momentum.

High-level response: we can support a move to a higher committed throughput and an expanded burst pocket. To get you a concrete proposal I want to confirm two items:
- steady-state monthly commit target (you listed 90M tokens) and whether you expect linear month-to-month growth or a seasonal spike pattern;
- acceptable latency SLOs per route (p95 target) and whether any routes are latency-critical (recommend those be pinned to dedicated capacity).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I'll put together commercial options for 90M/month (12-month term) and a stepped plan (90M -> 140M with staged discounts) so you can see the unit economics.
2) Karthik (cc'd) will join a technical call to walk through routing, rate limits, and how prefix/KV caching can reduce realized token spend.
3) Hannah will scope an SOW template and note any billing/PO fields we need.

Ballpark (high level) — subject to finalize: 90M/month committed gets a baseline unit rate, with a 6–12% discount on committed token spend if you commit 12 months. Burst pockets can be purchased as a separate monthly buffer (we typically size at 1.5–2x month for seasonal peaks) or as a short-term emergency burst credit you draw from. We'll surface a couple of approaches in the proposal.

I'll target a commercial + ops outline for Friday EOD. In the meantime can you share an expected monthly usage profile (avg + 95th pct) for July–December? That will help sizing.

Scheduling: I'm free Thu 6/5 at 10:00am PT or Fri 6/6 at 2:00pm PT for the 30m sync with Karthik. What works?

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Hosted API renewal — request to raise monthly throughput and burst window

Asha — thanks for looping us in. Quick technical sketch ahead of the call:

1) Rate limits & routing
- We can expose per-route RPS and per-tenant token-per-second ceilings. For a 90M/month commit, realistic sustained TPS is ~35–45 tokens/sec depending on average request size; for latency-critical endpoints we recommend pinning to dedicated capacity which eliminates noisy-neighbor variance.

2) Burst design
- Option A: monthly burst pocket (pre-purchased credits) sized at 1.5x committed month. This is simpler for procurement and results in predictable billing.
- Option B: on-demand burst with soft-throttle tiers (preferred for cost efficiency) — we allow higher throughput up to 4x for short windows but bill at a premium rate and guarantee fallbacks to lower-cost routes if sustained.

3) Cost & discount mechanics
- Commercial note: we can offer a 10% committed-spend discount for a 12-month extension on the new commit level (90M). If Parklane wants a stepped ladder to 140M over the year we can stage rate breaks at 110M and 140M with 6% and 12% effective discounts respectively.

4) Ops & SLOs
- We can commit to region-based latency SLOs: p95 < 220ms for hosted routes on recommended instance types; with dedicated capacity we can drive p95 < 120ms.

I've attached an ops worksheet and a simple QoS matrix to illustrate how we map routes to capacity classes. I'll bring these to the call.

Proposed meeting slots: Thu 6/5 10:00am PT or Fri 6/6 2:00pm PT. If one of those works I will send a calendar invite and prep a short runbook.

Quick answers to your asks:
- We'll commit to 90M tokens/month as the base for the 12-month term and evaluate staged increases in Q4.
- Expected usage profile: steady ~35M tokens/month now, projected climb to 75–100M in Oct–Dec with concentrated spikes on Black Friday (3–4x baseline for short bursts). I'll share a CSV with month-by-month projections after this thread.
- Latency critical endpoints: personalization inference is latency-sensitive; we'll want p95 targets below 160ms if possible — please confirm whether dedicated capacity is required to meet that consistently.

Please send the updated SOW and a redlined contract for our procurement and legal to review. We will also need a draft invoice with PO fields so our finance team can prepare a PO.

Looking forward to Friday.
